summary: Landry et al. 2017 meta-analysis (ALE) of neuroimaging of hypnosis: few reliable brain patterns emerge across studies; the only consistent correlate is activation in the lingual gyrus (visual imagery), NOT the hypothesized DMN/SN/CEN networks.
content: Landry et al. (2017) systematic review + ALE meta-analysis of hypnosis neuroimaging. Found 'few reliable brain patterns emerge across studies.' The hypothesized involvement of the executive (CEN), salience (SN), and default (DMN) networks was NOT confirmed; instead hypnosis correlated with activation of the lingual gyrus, a region involved in higher-order visual processing and mental imagery. The authors discuss this as the 'lowest common denominator' across studies.
